source.title: What is Intrinsic Motivation? A Typology of Computational Approaches

confidence_rationale: This is the canonical source that MECH-314's typology (novelty / info-gain / learning-progress sub-flavours) is organised around, and the direct namesake of MECH-314c (learning_progress_curiosity). Very high source quality (foundational, thousands of citations, defines the field's vocabulary). Mapping fidelity is high because REE's three-way MECH-314/314a/314c split IS Oudeyer & Kaplan's typology re-expressed; the caveat is that Oudeyer & Kaplan derive learning-progress as the reward signal that provably avoids the two failure modes REE's Phase-1 broadcast-scalar instantiation does NOT yet avoid.
failure_signatures: Prediction-error / novelty maximization (MECH-314a-like) drives the agent to unlearnable stochastic regions -- the 'noisy TV' / white-noise trap -- because raw unpredictability is maximal where nothing can be learned.
Predictability-maximization (the dual: seek maximally predictable states) collapses the agent onto trivial, already-mastered regions -- the 'blank wall' trap.

Only the DERIVATIVE (rate of change of predictive error = learning progress), not the level of error or novelty, tracks genuine competence acquisition; a scalar novelty/PE bonus without the derivative is vulnerable to both traps.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Intrinsic motivations can be organised into a formal typology within the RL reward framework. The most robust exploration driver is not novelty or prediction error per se but LEARNING PROGRESS -- the rate at which the agent's predictive model improves in a region. An agent that rewards itself for maximizing expected reduction in prediction error (the IAC / R-IAC algorithm) self-organises a developmental curriculum: it avoids both perfectly-predictable and perfectly-unpredictable regions and spends time exactly where it is currently learning fastest.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-314c (learning_progress_curiosity_intrinsic_motivation_analog) is REE's registration of exactly this signal: a bonus tracking |PE_t - PE_{t-K}| (rate-of-improvement) rather than PE level (MECH-314) or recency-of-encounter (MECH-314a). Oudeyer & Kaplan supply the theoretical justification for WHY MECH-314c should be preferred over its two sibling sub-flavours as the competence-earning driver, and the developmental-curriculum result is the mechanism WS-1 needs: an agent that cannot yet forage should be pulled toward the sub-tasks it is currently improving at, bootstrapping capability before structure is loaded.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Oudeyer & Kaplan's learning-progress is computed PER REGION (a partition of sensorimotor space, R-IAC) with a dedicated meta-predictor of error-reduction, and it drives a goal/region-SELECTION policy. REE Phase-1 MECH-314c is a single BROADCAST SCALAR (global e3._running_variance derivative) applied uniformly to all K candidates -- it therefore cannot yet build the regional curriculum that gives Oudeyer & Kaplan's result its force. The support is for the CLAIM (learning progress is the right signal) and directly motivates a per-region/per-candidate Phase-2 upgrade; it is NOT evidence the current broadcast-scalar substrate realises the developmental-curriculum behaviour.
mapping.source_context: Computational RL framework + developmental-robotics simulations and the Playground Experiment (a physical robot on a baby-mat autonomously structuring its own exploration into developmental stages via learning progress). No REE substrate; the transfer is architecture-to-architecture within the same RL reward formalism.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality maximal: this is the paper the MECH-314 typology is built on. Mapping fidelity high but capped below 0.85 because REE's broadcast-scalar Phase-1 does not yet instantiate the per-region learning-progress that carries the developmental-curriculum result. Transfer risk moderate: the formalism is RL-native (same frame as REE), but the load-bearing behaviour was shown on partitioned sensorimotor spaces REE has not built.
